text:
The first time I went in to use my Gold Card privileges for a dental scaling, the dentist was very accommodating. Then, on my way back, the staff member asked if I wanted to schedule a filling. I agreed, saying I wanted to use my Gold Card privileges. However, when I went to my second appointment, the staff member said I couldn't use my Gold Card privileges and would have to pay for it myself (why didn't they tell me this beforehand when they called to confirm the appointment so I wouldn't waste my time?). They gave the reason that it was a tooth I'd had previously had surgery on, so the clinic wouldn't be able to reimburse me (something I'd never know, even when I looked online for information). The staff member then said it had to be more than six months before I could get it done. When it was past six months, I called to schedule a filling, but the staff member said they weren't sure if I was eligible, using very rude language.

**** The clinic's response was completely untrue. ****
1) On October 10th, I didn't request a filling. I had scheduled a scaling first, and then consulted with the dentist about the missing filling (tooth #26). After the scaling, I scheduled a filling for tooth #26 on October 16th, stating that I wanted to use my Gold Card privileges. (as shown in the appointment slip) and the staff didn't inform me that I couldn't use my rights to fill the same tooth.
2) On October 15th, the staff called to confirm the appointment, but didn't provide any further information (as shown in the call history).
3) On October 16th, when I arrived at the clinic and handed over my ID card, saying I was here for my appointment (I hadn't even scanned my ID card yet), the staff member retorted that I couldn't use my Gold Card rights and that patients had to pay for it themselves if they wanted to have it done. (They probably wanted to force me to pay for it themselves.) So I asked why they hadn't informed me yesterday when they called to confirm the appointment that I couldn't use my Gold Card rights. And let me reiterate, the staff member didn't recommend filling the other problematic tooth, but I was the one who said, "Well, I can do it on another tooth." The staff member seemed reluctant, saying the spot was still small and to save my rights for another time. Before leaving, they told me to go back to my original clinic, or that if I wanted to have it done at this clinic, I had to wait until after 6 months for the clinic to reimburse me (the staff member said this). So I left without doing anything.
4) On November 17th (after 6 months, as advised by the staff member), I called to make an appointment to have my tooth filled. But the staff member said in an irritated tone, "If you insist on doing this, and if you can't enter the data, you'll have to pay for it yourself." (Even though the staff member had said it would take more than six months.) If the staff member said it definitely couldn't be done, why should I call?

I'm saying goodbye to this clinic. (I came here because it's close to my house.) The staff member was blunt and unreliable, and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone.
